slides.0.title: Weinviertel, Wagram, Carnuntum and Thermenregion
slides.0.subtitle: The other four Niederösterreich DACs
slides.1.title: Weinviertel: the first DAC
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Historic role
slides.1.highlights.0.content: From the 2002 vintage, approved in 2003: the first DAC in Austria
slides.1.highlights.1.title: A single variety
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Grüner Veltliner only, with the typical peppery, spicy character
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Klassik and Reserve
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Klassik at least 12% and Reserve at least 13% (Reserve from 2009)
slides.1.content: Weinviertel is known for peppery Grüner and is one of Austria's largest regions.
slides.2.title: Wagram and Carnuntum
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Wagram DAC
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Became a DAC in 2021; centred on loess terrain and Grüner Veltliner (Roter Veltliner is a local speciality)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Carnuntum DAC (2019)
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Whites: Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Grüner Veltliner; reds: Blaufränkisch, Zweigelt
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Carnuntum red rules
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Reds at least 12.0% abv; blends need at least two thirds from those varieties
slides.2.content: Carnuntum is a red-led DAC that also sets white rules.
slides.3.title: Thermenregion: 2023
slides.3.highlights.0.title: One of the newest DACs
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Became a DAC in 2023, south of Wien
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Alcohol thresholds
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Gebietswein and Ortswein at least 12%, Riedenwein at least 12.5%
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Residual sugar in red Rieden
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Red Riedenwein may have at most 4 g/L residual sugar
slides.3.content: These figures are recent; cross-check them against the official ÖWM rules.
Which single variety does Weinviertel DAC allow?
Weinviertel DAC is limited to Grüner Veltliner.
Which two varieties are used for Carnuntum DAC reds?
Carnuntum reds are Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt.
